Welcome
Wootton Bassett Infants’ School is situated in the heart of the community and is renowned for its caring and family atmosphere. ‘ Children enjoy learning a wide range of subjects and take part in a range of exciting experience that makes learning memorable. There is a calm and orderly atmosphere in lessons and around the school and pupils have positive attitudes and are keen to learn. The school has been relentless in their drive to improve the quality of education and leaders are aspirational for all pupils, including those with SEND’
'Wootton Bassett Infants' School is a "kind and friendly school.....where everyone is welcome' (OFSTED JANUARY 2023).
100% of our parents say 'My child is happy at this school' and 97% would recommend us to another parent
We encourage all our children to become confident and caring individuals and we help them to develop a lifelong love of learning.
We provide a diverse and creative curriculum with a wide range of first hand experiences to develop creative thinking and a thirst for new experiences.
We welcome diversity and encourage all our children to understand the contribution they can make to the community and wider society.
We recognise every child as a unique individual and nurture them to enable them to achieve. It is our aim that children leave Wootton Bassett Infants' School with lasting and fond memories of their time here. After all ……learning should be fun!
Mrs A Pass, Headteacher

Our Ethos, Values and Vision
Both Governors and staff have definite aims with regards to the children who will be in our care and these underpin the whole ethos of the school that we want to create.
Parents are encouraged to work in partnership with us in the development of their child, thus strengthening the bond between school and home life.
Our school values are:-
We want your child to take with them lasting and fond memories of their time at Wootton Bassett Infants, after all....

First hand experiences
We aim to equip the future generation with the knowledge and cultural capital they need to succeed as educated citizens in modern day society with sound judgement and strong core values which will enable them to thrive, be safe, and be the best that they can be. Our intention is for every child to leave us well prepared with a broad skillset, interest in the world around them, and a range of life-long learning experiences which will inspire them throughout their future education and beyond, contributing positively within our community.
Curriculum Aims and Intent
The aims of our school curriculum are to enable children to:
· have equal access to a rich, broad, balanced and immersive curriculum
· increase their knowledge, skills and understanding as they grow and develop and strengthen their connections with the world around them
· make good progress in the development of their learning with language and vocabulary at the core.
· engage the children’s interest
· develop their growing knowledge, skills and understanding of the world
· open their eyes to awe and wonder and cause them to marvel at the incredible and fantastic world in which they live
· develop their talents, skills and a love of learning.
To ensure this happens we will:
· execute a curriculum that is creative, carefully planned and structured
· offer an ambitious, cross curricular and topic- based curriculum with quality texts at its heart
· provide pupils with a range of first-hand experiences
· provide all pupils with equal access to a rich, broad, balanced and inclusive curriculum
· offer excellent opportunities to extend creative learning, challenge their imagination, value originality and to encourage and motivate them to want to learn.
· provide a wealth of opportunities to immerse children in the world around them
· reinforce their learning and underpin their growing knowledge, skills and understanding of the world
· engage with the local community through local area visits,
· engage with different cultural and generational groups and support local charities.

Prospective Parents
Starting school for the first time can be daunting for children and parents alike. Here at Wootton Bassett Infants' School we strive to make the transition as easy as possible.
We understand choosing a school for your little one can be a daunting task so we welcome visits from prospective parents and carers all year round. To arrange a visit and chat with either Mrs Pass, Headteacher please call 01793 852254 or email admin@woottonbassett-inf.wilts.sch.uk.
Open Events for Intake September 2027 - TBC dates and times will be published here when available.
Our school brochure is divided into two sections
Part 1 - An Introduction to Wootton Bassett Infants' School (updated for Sept 2026)
Part 2 - The Curriculum
Applications are made through Wiltshire Council Admissions portal here: Admissions (wiltshire.gov.uk)
Information for School Starters
It is an exciting time for parents preparing for their child to start school in Reception. However, this excitement can often be met with worry, as uncertain times can raise questions and worries. The way we talk about this transition can play an important role in helping you and your child feel reassured and confident. To help answer questions and find the best ways to support your child we would like to share with you a dedicated website: https://startingreception.co.uk/. It includes information for creating healthy routines, tips for preparing you and your child, how to support additional needs, brushing their teeth, potty training and so much more.
You can also find details of recommended vaccinations before your child starts school CLICK HERE and uniform is purchased through myclothing.com.
Here's a song to listen to with your child about the steps of starting school. MCGrammar - Steps for School Song
Best Start in Life - Cracking Communication
‘The Best Start in Life Strategy 2025 focuses on supporting children from pregnancy to age
five through integrated family services, early education, and health support to ensure
every child can thrive.’
The strategy recognises that the early years are a crucial time in a child’s development. Its aim is to make sure every family—no matter their circumstances—can access the right help at the right time. This includes parenting support, health guidance, and high‑quality early education. Together, these help children build the communication, emotional, and social skills they need to feel confident and ready for school.
At Wootton Bassett Infant School, we fully embrace these principles and are committed to supporting each child’s early development so they can flourish from the very beginning.
Giving every child the best start in life - GOV.UK
🌱 Helping Your Child Build Strong Communication Skills
The early years are a vital time for developing speaking, listening and interaction.
🤝 Working in Partnership with Parents
Parents have told national services they often struggle to find reliable guidance about child development. The strategy aims to make information clearer and easier to access.
🎓 High‑Quality Teaching in the Early Years
The strategy highlights the importance of well‑trained, confident staff who understand how young children learn.
💛 Supporting Children Who Need Extra Help
Reducing inequalities and supporting disadvantaged families is a key priority.
· We are recognised as an ‘Affordable school’ and everything we do in school is implemented through the lens of affordability. We have a designated email address affordability@woottonbassett-inf.wilt.sch.uk where you can share financial challenges or concerns on a confidential platform.
· Our staff are trained in the ‘Five to Thrive’ approach.
· Our SEN provision map shows what is available for all children but also how we can support specific and additional needs.
🎒 Helping Families Prepare for School
Many parents feel unsure about what “school‑ready” means. The Best Start in Life campaign aims to provide simple, clear guidance.
We have an experienced, enthusiastic EYFS team.
We have a designated wellbeing lead.
We’re Here to HelpEvery family’s journey is different. If you have questions or would like support with any part of your child’s early development, please speak to us—we’re always happy to help.
© Wootton Bassett Infants' School

Noremarsh
As an Infants School, our Year 2 children leave us at the end of the summer term and start at a Junior School the following September.
Most of the children go to Noremarsh Junior School which is part of the ASCEND Learning Trust. As a result, you must apply for a Year 3 place for your child, it is not a straight move. Details are sent out on how to apply nearer the time.
Throughout the year we combine with Noremarsh for events to ensure the transition for our Year 2 children is as smooth as possible. In the past we have visited the school for an Easter Egg hunt, Sports Day and Fun Activities.
